```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(RcmdrShiny)
```

The Wave 6.5 menu platform replaces the positional Rcmdr menu tree with a
curated, multi-level menubar. The statistical commands are unchanged; only the
layout and the interface identifiers change.

## Inspect the tree

```{r tree}
tree <- menu_tree()
vapply(tree, function(node) node$label, character(1))
```

Each group carries a `menu_id`; each leaf carries an `item_id`, a stable DOM
key and the original `command`:

```{r leaves}
leaves <- menu_leaves(tree)
head(leaves[, c("item_id", "menu_id", "command", "path")], 5)
```

A dialogue, the palette and the history still use the command id. The stable
item id is what the DOM, favourites and tests can rely on when the menu is
reordered.

## One Save, many formats

```{r save}
save <- leaves[grepl("^File > Save", leaves$path), c("item_id", "label",
                                                      "command")]
save
```

## Validate a fragment

```{r validate}
registry <- RcmdrShiny:::menu_registry_load(
  RcmdrShiny:::menu_registry_default_file(), module = "core"
)
RcmdrShiny:::menu_registry_validate(registry)$ok
```

The validator checks unique ids, existing parents, cycles and command
references. First-party module fragments live in
`plugins/<module>/inst/menus/module.yml` and are merged after the core.

## Migrate old preferences

Expanded menu ids are migrated on load:

```{r migration}
RcmdrShiny:::menu_migrate_ids(c("fileMenu", "statisticsMenu", "modelsMenu"))
```

Favourites and recents remain keyed by the stable command id, so they survive
the layout change without a mapping.

## Module contract

The first-party modules are versioned with the application. A module fragment
declares groups and items with `module_id`, `menu_id` and `item_id`; it may
remove individual core commands it replaces, but it does not delete a whole
core menu. This keeps the help centre, tour and diagnostics available in every
module combination.
